subject: Educational Psychology
stem: L.L. Thurstone proposed that intelligence consists not of one general factor but of several independent 'Primary Mental Abilities' such as:

options.option_text: Verbal comprehension, numerical ability, spatial visualisation, memory, reasoning

explanation: Thurstone identified around seven distinct Primary Mental Abilities (verbal, numerical, spatial, memory, reasoning, perceptual speed, word fluency) — directly challenging Spearman's single 'g' factor model.

explanation: Guilford's cube model has three dimensions — Operations (mental processes), Content (type of information), and Products (form the information takes) — yielding a large number of distinct intellectual abilities.

explanation: An IQ of 100 is defined as the statistical average/median. Scores well above (roughly 130+) are considered gifted/very superior; scores well below (roughly under 70) may indicate intellectual disability.

stem: Raymond Cattell distinguished between 'fluid intelligence' (novel problem-solving ability) and 'crystallised intelligence', which refers to:

options.option_text: Accumulated knowledge and skills gained through experience and education
Pure reflex reactions with no learning involved
Physical strength unrelated to any mental ability

explanation: Crystallised intelligence is knowledge and skill built up through learning and experience (vocabulary, general knowledge), generally holding steady or increasing with age — unlike fluid intelligence (novel reasoning), which tends to decline later in life.
